Summary



Hatch engineering culture is driven by speed, ownership, and impact. We're a small, ambitious team building AI that  transforms how service businesses grow, and we move fast. Engineers own problems end to end, ship to production early, and work across a modern stack (Elixir, Python, Go, React + TypeScript) on problems that directly shape the customer experience. At the end of the day, we're here to build something that matters, grow as engineers, and do it together.



The Forward Deployed Engineer is a first-class builder who ships production code into Hatch's core codebase, internal tooling, and the integration layer that connects Hatch's products to client systems. The primary focus is Hatch's Voice AI product: real-time voice agents that answer calls, qualify leads, and book appointments directly against clients' CRM and field-service systems.



"Forward deployed" describes where you work, not the caliber of what you build. You sit close to our most strategic clients, watch their real call traffic, and debug their failures yourself, working through agent traces, LLM tool-call payloads, service logs, and the client's own API until you can name the actual defect. Then you fix it where it belongs: in the client's configuration, in the integration layer, or in Hatch's core voice pipeline so every customer gets the fix.



Most of your week looks like engineering: reading traces, writing repros, instrumenting what nobody measured, shipping PRs, and validating them on production traffic. The rest is being the person both our clients and our Product team trust on the technical detail. You'll be deep in the build, held to production-grade standards, and given a genuine seat at the R&D table.



This opportunity requires you to be located in the United States.



We’d love to have you apply, even if you don’t feel you meet every single requirement in this posting. At Hatch, we’re looking for great people, not just those who simply check off all the boxes.



What you'll do



 - Root-cause voice AI failures and ship fixes into the core product. Start from one bad call and work backward through agent spans, tool-call arguments, application logs, and warehouse queries until you can explain exactly what happened. Then push PRs into Hatch's voice pipeline and integration layer, gate risky changes behind feature flags, and confirm on live traffic that the fix actually fires.

 - Build and extend the integration layer. Direct API integrations, webhook endpoints, event-driven triggers, and connectors for CRMs and scheduling systems that have no Hatch integration yet. Reconcile what a client's business needs against what their API actually returns, including the cases where those two disagree.

 - Build the tooling and instrumentation that makes this repeatable. Local simulators, harnesses that replay production calls end-to-end, behavioral test suites that catch regressions before a rollout, plus the spans, metrics, and dashboards that separate good calls from bad ones. Know when something you built breaks before the customer does. Build it to first-class standards even when no client ever sees it.

 - Work in the model layer. Prompt structure and guardrails, A/B comparisons between models on real traffic, tradeoffs across latency, cost, and quality, and the practical limits (context budgets, rate limits, tool-calling reliability) that decide whether a design survives production.

 - Own technically complex onboardings end-to-end and serve as the primary technical consultant for clients. Multi-system orchestrations, custom business logic, and CRMs with no connector, while always looking for the reusable pattern underneath. Includes potential onsite visits to present architectural solutions and see deployments through.

 - Turn implementation learnings into product. Surface the recurring patterns that justify dedicated R&D investment, and where something belongs natively, build the first-class version yourself and hand it off to an R&D team to own.
   
   

What it takes to succeed

 - 1-4 years of software engineering experience. You take systems apart to see how they actually work, you'd rather read the source or the raw API response than guess, and debugging is one of your core skills. You're comfortable being handed one broken production interaction with no stack trace and expected to come back with the cause.

 - Proven ability to navigate a broad technology ecosystem and comprehensive developer documentation. You can tell the difference between a problem that warrants a change to Hatch's core code and one that should live in middleware or automation tooling.

 - You verify in production and hold yourself to a high bar. Anyone can find a plausible explanation; you confirm it against real data before calling it fixed. Because you ship quickly and with real autonomy, correctness is on you. Implementations should be right, not just working: complete and consistent, not merely functional.

 - Great communication with business and technical audiences. When requirements are ambiguous, you resolve them before building, not after. You give clear, proactive status updates on your active builds: where you are, what's blocking you, and what the customer needs to know technically. You own the technical work and the client relationship, not project management.

 - You get real leverage out of AI coding tools. You use them to move faster on investigation, tooling, and implementation, and you still own the correctness of everything you ship.

 - Experience with voice AI is not required. Having shipped LLMs into a real application is a bonus: prompt design, tool calling and orchestration, evals, and the failure modes that only show up under real traffic. Familiarity with the voice stack is a further plus, but it's learnable on the job and we expect to teach it.
   
   

What you'll get

 - Based on the anticipated level of experience we are seeking, we expect the compensation range for this role to be between $144,000 and $200,000

 - Full responsibility for projects from day one, a collaborative team, and a dynamic work environment.

 - This opportunity has the option to be fully remote in all locations across the US

 - Effective your first day: Full medical, vision, and dental

 - Mental health support and services via Modern Health

 - 15 days PTO (accrual begins on date of hire and increases with 2+ years of tenure thereafter), 12 paid holidays, plus one floating holiday

 - Up to 14 weeks of parental leave

 - Monthly wellness stipend

 - 401(k) retirement savings plan

 - Employee stock purchase plan

 - Professional development reimbursement

 - Work from home reimbursement



Why Hatch

 - Shape the future of AI-driven customer service

 - Build alongside founders and leaders who value speed, ownership,and ambition

 - Solve challenging problems and see the impact on real businesses and customers

 - Join a team of builders who care about great engineering, fast execution, and each other

* Operate and maintain Kubernetes clusters that run our inference workloads

* Participate in a shared on-call rotation and incident response

* Familiarity with Linux and command line tools

* Experience with Docker and Kubernetes

**Description**
Do you want to protect how Amazon's workforce signs in and accesses critical systems every day? Amazon Foundational Security Services is looking for a Software Development Engineer II to build and operate the identity and authentication services that keep tens of thousands of employees secure and productive. You'll design and deliver distributed systems that handle real-time identity data sync, certificate issuance for corporate devices, and Kerberos authentication—solving problems where correctness and availability matter around the clock.
  
  
This role offers rare breadth across the identity space in one team. You'll work on workforce sign-in and AWS access, near real-time directory sync, a corporate certificate authority, and Kerberos authentication. You'll balance building new capabilities on AWS with modernizing long-running core infrastructure, all through a security-first lens. If you're ready to turn well-understood business problems into simple, secure, and maintainable code while learning from every incident and mentoring others, we'd love to hear from you.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design and build distributed services that handle authentication, authorization, and identity data synchronization, making sound tradeoffs between scalability, performance, and security
* Deliver software features across the full lifecycle—from scoping and design through code, testing, deployment, and maintenance—while actively reviewing code and providing meaningful feedback to teammates
* Participate in operational support including oncall rotation, monitoring and alarming, root cause analysis, and balancing new feature work against operational improvements to ensure services remain reliable
* Work with identity and security technologies such as SAML, OpenID Connect, SCIM, LDAP, Active Directory, Kerberos, and X.509 certificates to solve real authentication and authorization challenges
* Document how your services are constructed, tested, operated, and secured, and train new team members so they can confidently contribute and maintain the systems you build

A day in the life
  
  
Most days start with a short standup. You might spend the morning drafting a design doc for speeding up group membership sync for very large groups, then write and test the code with help from AI coding assistants. You review teammates' code and designs, offering constructive feedback. In the afternoon, you might pair with a newer engineer or meet with a partner team that depends on your identity data to understand their next requirements. During your oncall week, you triage alarms and tickets, identify root causes, and implement permanent fixes.
  
  
**About The Team**
We're part of Amazon Foundational Security Services within Amazon Security. Our team builds and operates the identity and authentication services Amazon's workforce uses every day—from signing in and accessing AWS, to syncing identity data across downstream systems, to issuing certificates for corporate devices. We're based in Seattle and share oncall across the team, learning from every incident through structured post-incident reviews.
  
  
Mentorship is part of the job here. Engineers get broad exposure to identity, security, and AWS, and grow by owning real problems end to end. Whether you're ramping up on our systems or taking on harder, more ambiguous challenges as you progress toward Software Development Engineer III, you'll find a team that supports your growth and values operational excellence alongside innovation.
  
  
Diverse Experiences

experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

**About Baseten**
Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.
  
  
**THE ROLE**
Every agent on Baseten Sandboxes gets its own microVM, where it writes and runs code, calls tools, and keeps state across long tasks. Agents pause and resume constantly, so the machine underneath has to start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume fast, and keep every tenant isolated while it does. General-purpose virtualization was not built for that workload.
  
  
The Agent Infra team builds that layer. Sandboxes run in microVMs with custom Linux kernels on bare-metal servers we operate. You'll own how sandboxes start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume, and how they perform on each host's CPU and memory, down to the hardware. You'll also own the guest and host side of each sandbox: its identity, how it attaches to different storage classes for performance or capabilities, and the virtual devices that connect it securely to the network. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel, whose microVM sandboxes are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes.
  
  
We are building a cloud, not just using one. That means designing for many tenants from day one and thinking through what each decision means all the way down to the datacenter. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs.
  
  
If you've worked deep in KVM and Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, or QEMU and want to build the computers AI agents run on, we'd love to talk.

* Baseten Sandboxes documentation

* Own the microVM lifecycle for agent sandboxes: start, stop, suspend, resume, snapshot, and fork
* Build and tune the custom guest kernels sandboxes run on
* Tune host CPU and memory configuration so sandboxes run fast and safely on each type of hardware we operate
* Manage host-level resources and sandbox density on each machine
* Own startup and resume performance end to end, from VM boot or snapshot restore to the first command
* Own the guest and host side of each sandbox: its identity, how it attaches to storage, and the virtual devices that connect it to the network
* Design isolation for multi-tenant workloads where the hypervisor is the security boundary
* Debug virtualization and isolation issues at scale, from userspace through the kernel to the hardware
* Contribute architecture decisions and code back to the open-source projects we build on

* Deep understanding of Linux internals: namespaces, cgroups, memory management, and the boot path
* Experience building cloud infrastructure as the provider (multi-tenant compute that customers run on), not only running workloads on a cloud provider
* Experience building multi-tenant infrastructure where isolation is a security boundary
* Strong systems programming background in Rust and/or Go; C/C++ also welcome
* Experience debugging performance and correctness problems across userspace and kernel boundaries

Every agent on Baseten Sandboxes runs in its own microVM. Agents call models, reach tools and APIs, expose services, and more and more often talk to each other. This role is separate from Baseten's GPU-to-GPU networking. Here you'll own how sandboxes connect to each other, to Baseten services, to customer networks, and to the internet.

**THE ROLE**
Storage decides how fast agent sandboxes start and how safely they share data. Agents need a filesystem that thousands of sandboxes mount at the same time, with strict isolation and the consistency agents need. Agent context is mostly small files, so the access patterns look very different from storage built for large files.
  
  
The Agent Infra team builds Agent Drive, the distributed filesystem that agent sandboxes mount over FUSE, and the storage underneath it. The work uses tiered caching, replication, content-addressed data, and Linux filesystem internals. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel, whose sandboxes and Agent Drive filesystem are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes.
  
  
We are building a cloud, not just using one, so storage is designed for many tenants from day one. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs.
  
  
If you care about page cache coherency, FUSE, replication protocols, and content-addressable storage, we'd love to talk.
  
  
**EXAMPLE INITIATIVES**

* Blaxel is joining Baseten to build the future of agentic infrastructure
* Baseten Sandboxes documentation

**Responsibilities**

* Design and implement core Agent Drive features: metadata replication, volume placement, garbage collection, and FUSE client behavior
* Solve multi-attach correctness: cache coherency across many FUSE mounts of the same drive, dentry and inode invalidation, write ordering, and crash consistency
* Optimize tail latency on read and write paths, including page cache strategy, writeback, prefetch, and metadata RPC batching
* Build tenant isolation into the storage layer, including quota enforcement, blast-radius containment, and noisy-neighbor mitigation
* Own the storage side of sandbox startup and resume performance
* Build durable block storage for sandboxes alongside other Baseten storage teams
* Build observability into every layer, drive storage incidents end to end, and turn each one into a permanent fix
* Contribute upstream to the open-source storage projects we build on

**Requirements**

* Strong systems programming background in Go, Rust, and/or C/C++, with comfort reading kernel code
* Deep understanding of Linux filesystem and storage internals: VFS, page cache, dentry and inode caches, FUSE, the block I/O stack, fsync semantics, and crash consistency
* Hands-on experience building distributed storage systems, content-addressable storage, or large-scale caching infrastructure
* Experience profiling I/O, memory, and RPC bottlenecks and optimizing tail latency in production
* Ability to debug correctness bugs that only show up under concurrency or partial failure
* You move fast and like owning a problem end to end on a small team

**NICE TO HAVE**

* Experience with a distributed filesystem or object store such as JuiceFS, CephFS, or S3-compatible storage, or contributions to those projects
* Knowledge of consensus and replication protocols (Raft, leader leases, quorum reads)
* Experience with snapshot, clone, and copy-on-write filesystem features
* Experience operating multi-tenant storage with hard isolation requirements
* Familiarity with Linux performance tooling such as eBPF, io\_uring, perf, ftrace, and blktrace

Our engineers work directly with stakeholders, get close to customers' needs, and are empowered to take technical risks to build the best-in-class software with respect to quality, scale, and insights. The technical foundation this team builds, helps keep all of Amazon (Fulfillment Centers, Physical Stores, Whole Foods, Fresh, etc.) secure.
  
  
We need folks who have a passion for building hyper-scale systems that are always online. Those with an entrepreneurial spirit to take risks, experiment with new technical methods, and focus on improving what came before will find themselves perfectly at home in our team.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Architecture Design and Review
* Software Feature development in Java and Python using AWS services (S3, Lambda, SQS, Fargate/ECS, EMR, Spark, etc.)
* Setting and achieving a high bar for Operational Excellence.
* Earning trust in all directions; building partnerships with technical internal Amazon stakeholders WW.
* System resilience testing and preparation.
* Software project planning using Agile Methodologies (Scrum)

As a member of the team, your duties will range from system/software design, AWS configuration, software feature/library development, strategic technical planning, and partnering with several security and technical teams worldwide.  The Bot Management team within Traffic Engineering uses machine learning to separate human visitors from automated traffic and to detect and stop abusive bots in real time. You will take models from research into production, own them through training, evaluation, serving, and monitoring, and partner with Applied Scientists to continuously improve detection accuracy and system performance. **Role Summary**
We are hiring an AI Engineer to design, build, and operate agentic AI systems — LLM-powered agents that reason over enterprise data, call tools, and execute multi-step workflows end to end. This is a hands-on engineering role at the center of how we automate complex technical and operational work. You will take ambiguous problems, decompose them into agent workflows, and ship production services that engineering teams depend on daily.
  
This is an ideal role for an engineer with a strong Python and ML foundation who has already shipped LLM or RAG applications and now wants to go deeper into orchestration, tool-calling, and autonomous multi-agent architectures. You will work within an established platform and architecture, with senior engineers available for design review — but you will own your components from prototype through production.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities
  
Agent Design & Orchestration**

* Build and ship LLM-powered agents that plan, call tools, and complete multi-step tasks using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or equivalent orchestration libraries.
* Implement multi-agent workflows — planner, executor, reviewer, and specialist roles — including state handling, hand-off logic, retries, and graceful failure paths.
* Design and expose tools to agents via function-calling and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, wrapping internal APIs, databases, and enterprise systems as safe, well-scoped agent capabilities.

**Retrieval & Knowledge Systems**

* Build and operationalize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines: chunking, embedding, vector and hybrid search, re-ranking, and context assembly.
* Integrate structured, semi-structured, and unstructured sources — SharePoint, Confluence, Jira, REST APIs, Excel, and SQL warehouses — into retrieval and agent context layers.
* Continuously improve answer grounding and reduce hallucination through better retrieval, prompt design, and context management.

**Engineering & Deployment**

* Develop production Python services and APIs for agent and model inference using FastAPI, containerized with Docker and deployed through standard CI/CD pipelines.
* Instrument agents with tracing, token and cost accounting, latency monitoring, and structured logging so that behavior is observable and debuggable in production.
* Apply MLOps and LLMOps practices including version control for prompts and configs, automated regression testing, and safe rollout of model or prompt changes.

**Evaluation & Quality**

* Build evaluation harnesses for agent workflows — golden datasets, task-level success metrics, LLM-as-judge scoring, and regression suites that gate releases.
* Measure and tune for accuracy, latency, and cost, and make explicit trade-offs between them based on the use case.

**Collaboration**

* Partner with domain experts, data engineers, and product stakeholders to turn manual workflows into reliable automated agents.
* Deliver results through interfaces users actually adopt — Streamlit apps, chat interfaces, dashboards, and embedded integrations.
* Write clear design notes and runbooks, and participate actively in code and design reviews.

**Required Qualifications**

* 3-5 years of professional software, ML, or data engineering experience, including at least 1 year building LLM-based or GenAI applications.
* Strong Python engineering skills — not just notebooks. Production code, testing, packaging, async patterns, and API development with FastAPI or similar.
* Hands-on experience with at least one LLM orchestration framework (LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or an equivalent) in a shipped application.
* Demonstrated experience building RAG systems: embeddings, vector stores (e.g., FAISS, pgvector, Pinecone, Chroma), and retrieval quality tuning.
* Practical command of prompt engineering, structured output, function/tool calling, and context-window management.
* Working knowledge of SQL and cloud data platforms (Snowflake, Databricks, or equivalent), and comfort writing queries against enterprise schemas.
* Experience containerizing and deploying services with Docker and shipping through CI/CD on a major cloud (Azure, AWS, or GCP).
* Solid grounding in ML fundamentals and familiarity with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or HuggingFace Transformers.
* Clear written and verbal communication, and the judgment to escalate when a problem is under-specified rather than guessing.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience building or consuming Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, or comparable agent tool-integration layers.
* Production experience with multi-agent or agentic workflow systems, including human-in-the-loop checkpoints and approval gates.
* Familiarity with LLM observability and evaluation tooling such as LangSmith, Langfuse, Weights & Biases, or MLflow.
* Experience with workflow orchestration tools — Airflow, Dagster, Prefect — or analytics engineering with DBT.
* Exposure to model fine-tuning or parameter-efficient adaptation (LoRA/PEFT) and knowing when it is — and is not — the right answer.
* Background in a technical engineering domain (semiconductor, hardware validation, manufacturing, or similar) where agents operate over specialized data.
* Experience with AI governance, responsible-AI review, or enterprise security requirements for LLM deployments.

Build a Safer World.
  
  
TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.
  
  
As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will work directly with TRM's national-security customers — deploying our platform into their environments, sitting with the people who use it, and building what the mission actually needs.
  
  
This is a generalist engineering role. In a given quarter you might ship application code, debug a Kubernetes workload in a restricted environment, design a data schema, stand up cloud infrastructure, or prototype an entirely new capability because a customer described a problem nobody has solved yet. You will often be the only TRM engineer in the room. What you build enables our government customers to use TRM securely in the most demanding environments in the world — and carries what you learn there back into the product.
  
  
**The Impact You Will Have**

* Deploy, integrate and operate TRM's platform inside customer environments - cloud and air-gapped - and own the outcome, not just your slice of it.
* Sit directly with mission users, translate what they need into working software, and build it: integrations, data pipelines, and prototypes that prove out a capability before it's a product.
* Deliver across whatever the problem requires — application code, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, databases, data flow - rather than staying inside one specialty.
* Act as the technical bridge back to TRM's product and engineering teams, carrying mission context into the roadmap.
* Diagnose and resolve hard problems in constrained environments, with limited tooling and limited outside help.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Strong programming ability in Python and/or Node.js/TypeScript, with real fluency developing with AI — coding agents and LLM tooling are part of how you ship, and you have judgment about where they help and where they don't.
* Hands-on Kubernetes: deploying, debugging and reasoning about real workloads. Maintaining someone else's cluster is not the same thing.
* Production AWS experience — building environments, not just consuming them.
* Working fluency with relational databases (PostgreSQL or similar): schema design, query tuning, moving data around safely.
* Range. Concrete examples of delivering outside your primary specialty — a new language, datastore or platform you picked up because the project needed it.
* Outstanding written and verbal communication. You will be the only engineer in front of a customer regularly, and comfort there is not optional.

Bonus, not required — depth in any of these raises the bar
  
  

* Infrastructure as code (Terraform) and GitOps (Argo CD)
* Data engineering at scale — orchestration, streaming, columnar/analytics stores
* Distributed systems design and debugging
* Building machine learning or agentic systems
* Deep Linux/Unix and networking, especially in restricted or disconnected environments
* Prior delivery inside classified or otherwise regulated government environments

**About The Team**

* Small, senior and high-trust. Everyone owns a real surface end to end; nobody is handed a queue of tickets.
* We are the closest team at TRM to our customers, and we put them first. We do what it takes for their mission to succeed.
* We align to US-eastern hours, on-site and remote, and we communicate across a lot of channels — high-side chat, high-side and low-side email, Slack, phone, Signal, Google Meet — switching between them fast when the situation calls for it.
* Weekly team syncs plus project check-ins. We keep tracking current in Linear and raise problems the moment we see them rather than at the next standup.

**Learn About TRM Speed In This Position**

* Rapid issue resolution. FDEs identify and diagnose critical on-site issues, open an incident channel or virtual war room with the remote team, and land fixes in minutes to hours — then run the retro and share the lesson with internal and customer stakeholders within 48 hours.
* Navigating bureaucratic hurdles. FDEs anticipate customer-side delays rather than absorbing them: building relationships with customer stakeholders, finding the bottleneck, and finding another path to approval. Weeks of waiting become days.
* Efficient knowledge transfer. Documentation stays current in Notion and work stays current in Linear. Anything that threatens a milestone is flagged within 24 hours, so the remote team is never surprised.

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

**Description**
Annapurna Labs designs the silicon behind AWS machine learning acceleration. Trainium and Inferentia servers train and serve the largest models our customers run, and before any of that hardware carries customer traffic it has to prove it works. MLA Vetting owns that gate. We build the diagnostic tests that every accelerator server runs before it becomes sellable, and we decide which failures block a host, which route to a technician for repair, and which are noise.
  
  
That gate only works if we can see through it. We are hiring a Software Development Engineer II to build the data and analytics systems that tell us what our tests are actually doing across the fleet. You will build the pipelines that ingest diagnostic results from tens of thousands of servers, the dashboards that make test behavior legible, and the metrics and alarms that tell us a test has started failing on a hardware generation before it costs us a week of capacity. When the team decides whether a diagnostic has enough evidence to move from observation into blocking production, your data answers that question.
  
  
This is a software engineering role, not a reporting role. You will write and operate production code, own the alarms and metrics that page us, and build detection for trends nobody is watching yet. You will work directly with hardware, firmware, provisioning, and data center operations teams who act on what you build.
  
  
You are fluent in Python and SQL and have built production data pipelines at scale. Experience with Amazon Redshift, Apache Spark, workflow orchestration, and dashboarding in Grafana or QuickSight maps directly to what you will work on here. Experience with telemetry or diagnostic data from a large server fleet, or with defining metrics and anomaly detection on operational time-series data, will have you productive faster. Familiarity with server hardware or data center operations is a plus, not a requirement — we will teach you the hardware.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
Design, build, and operate production data pipelines that ingest diagnostic, telemetry, and repair-ticket data from the Trainium and Inferentia fleet into a warehouse other teams query with confidence.
  
  
Build and own the metrics, alarms, and anomaly detection that surface test regressions, failure-rate shifts, and new failure signatures across hardware generations without a human going looking for them.
  
  
Build dashboards and visualizations that make fleet and test health legible to engineers, hardware partners, and leadership, covering failure rates, failure-signature breakdowns, first pass yield, and repair latency.
  
  
Analyze large-scale fleet data to find root cause behind failure trends, and separate genuine hardware faults from software defects and test noise — a distinction that decides whether a failure reaches a technician or an engineer.
  
  
Define the evidence standard that gates operational decisions, including whether a diagnostic has soaked long enough and cleanly enough in the fleet to move from observation mode into blocking production.
  
  
Improve data quality and pipeline reliability so downstream consumers trust the numbers without re-deriving them.
  
  
Write clear analyses and design documents for technical and non-technical readers, including leadership.
  
  
A day in the life
  
  
You start by checking an alarm that fired overnight: a diagnostic's failure rate climbed on one server generation. You query the failure signatures, find the increase concentrates in one component and one data center, and hand the breakdown to the hardware team by mid-morning. The rest of the day goes to a pipeline you are building to join repair outcomes against diagnostic results, so the team can measure how often a repair actually fixes the fault it was dispatched for. You close the day reviewing a teammate's code review and answering an operations partner who needs a new cut of yield data.
  
  
**About The Team**
MLA Vetting sits between hardware manufacturing and customer-ready capacity. We own the diagnostic test suites and the triage framework that turn a raw hardware failure into a specific, actionable repair, and we own the fleet-scale evidence that drives hardware and firmware improvements upstream. Our work is measured in how fast a server reaches sellable and how often it gets there on the first try.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
* Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

**THE ROLE**
Storage decides how fast agent sandboxes start and how safely they share data. Agents need a filesystem that thousands of sandboxes mount at the same time, with strict isolation and the consistency agents need. Agent context is mostly small files, so the access patterns look very different from storage built for large files.
  
  
The Agent Infra team builds Agent Drive, the distributed filesystem that agent sandboxes mount over FUSE, and the storage underneath it. The work uses tiered caching, replication, content-addressed data, and Linux filesystem internals. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel, whose sandboxes and Agent Drive filesystem are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes.
  
  
We are building a cloud, not just using one, so storage is designed for many tenants from day one. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs.
  
  
If you care about page cache coherency, FUSE, replication protocols, and content-addressable storage, we'd love to talk.
  
  
**EXAMPLE INITIATIVES**

* Blaxel is joining Baseten to build the future of agentic infrastructure
* Baseten Sandboxes documentation

**Responsibilities**

* Design and implement core Agent Drive features: metadata replication, volume placement, garbage collection, and FUSE client behavior
* Solve multi-attach correctness: cache coherency across many FUSE mounts of the same drive, dentry and inode invalidation, write ordering, and crash consistency
* Optimize tail latency on read and write paths, including page cache strategy, writeback, prefetch, and metadata RPC batching
* Build tenant isolation into the storage layer, including quota enforcement, blast-radius containment, and noisy-neighbor mitigation
* Own the storage side of sandbox startup and resume performance
* Build durable block storage for sandboxes alongside other Baseten storage teams
* Build observability into every layer, drive storage incidents end to end, and turn each one into a permanent fix
* Contribute upstream to the open-source storage projects we build on

**Requirements**

* Strong systems programming background in Go, Rust, and/or C/C++, with comfort reading kernel code
* Deep understanding of Linux filesystem and storage internals: VFS, page cache, dentry and inode caches, FUSE, the block I/O stack, fsync semantics, and crash consistency
* Hands-on experience building distributed storage systems, content-addressable storage, or large-scale caching infrastructure
* Experience profiling I/O, memory, and RPC bottlenecks and optimizing tail latency in production
* Ability to debug correctness bugs that only show up under concurrency or partial failure
* You move fast and like owning a problem end to end on a small team

**NICE TO HAVE**

* Experience with a distributed filesystem or object store such as JuiceFS, CephFS, or S3-compatible storage, or contributions to those projects
* Knowledge of consensus and replication protocols (Raft, leader leases, quorum reads)
* Experience with snapshot, clone, and copy-on-write filesystem features

At the SEI AI Division, we conduct research in applied artificial intelligence and the engineering questions related to the practical design and implementation of AI technologies and systems. We currently lead a community-wide movement to mature the discipline of AI Engineering for Defense and National Security.
  
  
As our government customers adopt AI and machine learning to provide leap-ahead mission capabilities, we
  
  

* build real-world, mission-scale AI capabilities through solving practical engineering problems
* discover and define the processes, practices, and tools to support operationalizing AI for robust, secure, scalable, and human-centered mission capabilities
* prepare our customers to be ready for the unique challenges of adopting, deploying, using, and maintaining AI capabilities
* identify and investigate emerging AI and AI-adjacent technologies that are rapidly transforming the technology landscape

Are you creative, curious, energetic, collaborative, technology-focused, and hard-working? Are you interested in making a difference by bringing innovation to government organizations and beyond? Apply to join our team.
  
  
**Overview:**
As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will specialize in engineering solutions that support research into the vulnerabilities of AI and ML algorithms and securing against those vulnerabilities.
  
  
The Secure AI Lab within the SEI’s AI Division focuses on improving the security and robustness of AI systems. As part of the world-class research community at Carnegie Mellon University, the Secure AI Lab conducts and applies cutting-edge research to protect AI systems from adversaries who aim to manipulate the system to learn, do, or reveal something it isn’t supposed to.
  
  
The Secure AI Lab Consists Of Machine Learning Research Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, And Software Developers Who Work Together To Solve Problems In The Following Areas
  
  

* Counter AI Research: Study threat models targeting AI and ML algorithms, understand the behaviors of AI algorithms, identify weak points, and design novel ways to subvert AI and ML systems.
* AI and ML Algorithm Defense Research: Create practical mitigations and defenses for observed attacks affecting AI and ML algorithms and evaluate the effectiveness of defensive techniques.
* Applied Adversarial Machine Learning: Advance the state of the art in adversarial machine learning by developing and transitioning capabilities to government sponsors.

As an engineer, you will solve problems for government sponsors by analyzing, designing, and building responsible AI systems.
  
  
**Your Day-to-day Engineering Tasks Will Include**

* Identifying and investigating emerging AI and AI-adjacent technologies.
* Defining and refining processes, practices, and tools for working with AI.
* Designing and building well-engineered prototypes of AI systems.
* Transitioning and providing guidance on AI capabilities to government sponsors.

**Duties**

* Building Machine Learning Models and Systems: You will work with machine learning frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, Torch, and Caffe and modern programming languages including Python, C/C++, and Java. You will build and work with data pipelines, ETL processes, and backend systems. You will work with, extend, and implement state-of-the-art machine learning methods.
* Technical Experimentation: You will experiment with modern and emerging machine learning frameworks, methods, and algorithms in application domains that include computer vision, natural language processing, planning and scheduling, robot control, and engineering safe, trusted, and reliable machine learning systems.
* Testing and evaluation. You'll conduct rapid prototyping to demonstrate and evaluate technologies in relevant environments. You'll evaluate systems for performance and security. You'll test capabilities using novel testing and analysis techniques.
* Collaboration. You'll actively participate on teams of developers, researchers, designers, and technical leads. You'll collaborate with researchers and our government customers to understand challenges, needs, and possible solutions.
* Mentoring. You'll contribute to improving the overall technical capabilities of the Division by mentoring and teaching others, participating in design (software and otherwise) sessions, and sharing insights and wisdom across the SEI.

**Knowledge And Experience**

* Comprehensive knowledge of machine learning; previous experience in adversarial machine learning desirable but not required
* A track record of using well-established engineering practices to solve difficult problems

Stanbridge University is seeking
**Software Engineers – AI Systems (Go)**
to design, build, and operate production AI systems that perform complex, multi-stage work reliably and at scale.
  
  
This is a hands-on engineering role focused on a challenging class of problems: long-running AI workflows that call models, tools, and external APIs; maintain state across extended executions; produce structured content and generated media; interact with human reviewers; recover from partial failures; and consistently deliver accurate results to users.
  
  
The core engineering challenges extend well beyond prompt development. These systems must account for provider failures and rate limits, interrupted workflows, changing state, non-deterministic model behavior, incorrect or unsupported outputs, variable latency and cost, and deployments occurring while work is in progress.
  
  
The successful candidate will combine strong
**software and distributed-systems engineering judgment**
with practical experience building and operating
**LLM-backed applications, AI agents, or agent-based systems in production**
.
  
  
You will join at a stage where significant architecture remains to be designed and built. Engineers in this role will have substantial ownership over the patterns, services, infrastructure, and engineering standards that shape the University's AI systems.
  
  
**Remote Work Eligibility**
This position is eligible for remote work for candidates residing in states where Stanbridge University is currently authorized to employ remote employees. Eligible states currently include:
**Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Tennessee, Texas, and Wisconsin.**
Candidates must reside in an eligible state at the time of employment. Remote-work eligibility is subject to University employment requirements and may change based on applicable state requirements.
  
  
Engineering Environment
  
  
**The Engineering Problems Addressed By This Team Include**

* Durable workflow orchestration: Long-running, multi-stage pipelines using persistent state, job queues, checkpoints, resumability, idempotent execution, and recovery from interrupted or orphaned work.
* Multi-provider model infrastructure: Routing across commercial model providers with model registries, token and cost controls, rate-limit handling, retries, circuit breakers, health monitoring, and provider failover.
* Agent and tool orchestration: Systems in which AI agents interact with tools, APIs, data sources, application services, and deterministic business logic to complete multi-step work.
* Prompt engineering infrastructure: Treating prompts as version-controlled production artifacts with review, testing, regression protection, and measurable behavior.
* Testing non-deterministic systems: Recorded and replayable provider interactions, deterministic fixtures, evaluation harnesses, baselines, and regression testing for AI behavior.
* Correctness and quality controls: Structured-output validation, automated evaluation, domain-specific requirements, evidence checking, and safeguards against confident but incorrect model output.
* Human-in-the-loop workflows: Review and approval stages within automated processes, including systems capable of safely responding when users modify state or inputs during execution.
* Generated media pipelines: Systems capable of producing and managing documents, audio, imagery, video, and other generated assets.
* Production service architecture: Go-based APIs and backend services, relational data stores, job infrastructure, observability, and integrations supporting user-facing applications.
* Secure ingestion: Processing user-supplied and potentially untrusted documents while maintaining appropriate security and authorization boundaries.

Two Engineering Emphases
  
  
Engineers will meet the same overall technical bar but may bring deeper expertise in one of two areas:
  
  
Platform and Pipeline
  
  
Focused on distributed systems, workflow orchestration, durable state, job queues, recovery, provider infrastructure, latency, throughput, scalability, reliability, and cost optimization.
  
  
This emphasis is particularly well suited for experienced systems engineers who view AI models as powerful components that introduce a new set of distributed-systems and reliability challenges.
  
  
Agents and Quality
  
  
Focused on agent and tool architecture, prompt systems, context management, evaluation frameworks, regression testing, judge models, evidence validation, and end-to-end output quality.
  
  
This emphasis is particularly well suited for engineers who approach AI behavior through experimentation, measurement, testing, and systematic improvement.
  
  
Candidates may indicate an area of preference; however, specialization in one area is not required.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Design, develop, test, deploy, and operate production-quality software and backend services, primarily using Go (Golang).
* Architect and build AI agents and agent-based systems capable of using tools, interacting with APIs, maintaining state and context, and executing complex multi-step workflows.
* Design durable workflows that can checkpoint, resume, retry, recover, and safely continue execution following partial failures or system interruptions.
* Determine how models, agents, tools, APIs, data sources, services, and deterministic application logic should divide responsibilities within an AI system, including recognizing when an AI model is not the appropriate solution.
* Design integrations across multiple AI model providers, including routing, failover, rate-limit management, health monitoring, and degradation strategies.
* Build safeguards including structured-output validation, error handling, retries, quality gates, evidence validation, and automated recovery mechanisms.
* Develop testing strategies for non-deterministic AI behavior using techniques such as deterministic fixtures, recorded and replayed interactions, regression suites, evaluation harnesses, and quality baselines.
* Develop observability capabilities including tracing, metrics, logging, evaluation data, and replayable execution histories to support production debugging and performance analysis.
* Design human-in-the-loop workflows incorporating review, approval, intervention, and modification of workflow state.
* Build and maintain APIs, backend services, relational data models, job-processing infrastructure, and supporting application components.
* Develop secure methods for ingesting and processing user-supplied documents and other external content.
* Optimize systems for reliability, latency, throughput, scalability, output quality, and cost per execution.
* Build reusable engineering patterns and shared components that simplify the addition of new agents, model providers, tools, workflows, and output types.
* Own technical problems from initial investigation and architecture through implementation, deployment, monitoring, troubleshooting, and ongoing production operation.
* Collaborate directly with product stakeholders and domain experts to translate qualitative requirements into measurable system behavior and technical solutions.
* Contribute to architectural decisions and engineering standards for AI-powered applications across the University.

**Required**

* Hands-on experience shipping an LLM-backed application, AI agent, or agent-based system into production and supporting it after deployment.
* Strong understanding of AI application architecture, including how models, agents, tools, APIs, data sources, services, and application logic interact.

Key Responsibilities
  
  

* Design, modify, and implement software applications from functional and system design specifications.
* Code, integrate, test, debug, and refine software to produce secure, high-performing products.

* Build secure, versioned REST and gRPC APIs for object creation, retrieval, updates, and synchronization.
* Integrate established encryption, key-wrapping, and secret-management mechanisms.
* Prepare and review architecture, interface, design, and requirement documentation.
* Implement centralized logging, monitoring, audit trails, and end-to-end traceability for access events.
* Support the development and maintenance of software applications related to cybersecurity initiatives.

**Required Qualifications**
**Education:**
Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
  
  
**Experience:**
Five to ten years of software development experience, including GoLang programming in Linux environments and hands-on experience within cloud infrastructures.
  
  
**Technical Skills:**
Strong proficiency in object-oriented design, data structures, and secure software development practices. Demonstrated experience designing REST APIs, gRPC services, and networked client-server applications. Experience with structured data formats such as JSON and XML, as well as authentication, authorization, and role-based access control systems.
  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with cryptographic key management, certificate management, PKI, or secret-management systems.
* Working knowledge of AES, RSA, TLS/mTLS, key wrapping, initialization vectors, and related cryptographic concepts.
